rules.rule: CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED. Rounding is ROUND_HALF_EVEN (banker's) applied to the shortest-repr digit string. The original agent only tested USD cases where HALF_EVEN and HALF_UP mostly agree; I added 0-decimal-currency discriminators that isolate the mode unambiguously: JPY 0.5 -> ¥0, 1.5 -> ¥2, 2.5 -> ¥2, 3.5 -> ¥4. Negative values round symmetrically (magnitude half-even): JPY -0.5 -> -¥0, -1.5 -> -¥2, -2.5 -> -¥2; USD -0.125 -> -$0.12, -0.135 -> -$0.14. Works at any decimal count: BHD (3dp) 0.0125 -> BHD0.012, 0.0135 -> BHD0.014.
rules.jsNote: Round the digit STRING: keep `dp` fraction digits; look at the remainder. rest[0]>'5' => up; rest[0]=='5' && any nonzero after => up; exact tie => round up only if the last kept digit is odd. Apply to the ABSOLUTE value, then re-attach the sign (JPY -0.5 -> '-¥0' proves the sign survives a round-to-zero).

rules.rule: CONFIRMED. Python repr digits == JS Number.prototype.toString() digits; the scientific-notation threshold difference (Python exp>=16 / exp<-4 vs JS exp>=21 / exp<-6) is irrelevant because Decimal('1e+23') == Decimal('100000000000000000000000').
